children: , the global card and digital-payments network, teamed up with Mastercard and Ant International to build common standards for verifying AI purchasing agents, while its shares gained roughly 1.3% to $366.229 at 10.49am ET time on Thursday morning. The stock remains 9.38% below its GF Value estimate of $404.14, leaving a visible valuation gap despite the day's advance.

Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol gives approved AI agents signed credentials that merchants can recognize. That creates a clean dividing line between legitimate shopping assistants and hostile bots without forcing retailers or payment companies to rebuild the financial plumbing underneath every transaction.

AI agents may soon choose products, compare merchants and initiate purchases for consumers. Visa's opportunity is to keep control of the valuable layersauthorization, tokenization and fraud protectioneven when software makes the buying decision. The standards strengthen Visa's position, but the payoff depends on AI agents generating new payment volume instead of merely replacing transactions consumers already make.

title: Visa Share Rises as Payment Networks Standardize AI-Agent Identity
